sentences.text: A long, sweeping crescent of sand shelved gently into the sea, deserted from one headland to the other.
In the secluded, sheltered cove, small waves lapped at the shore as softly as breathing.
Powdery, bone-white sand shimmered in the heat until the far end of the bay seemed to dissolve into air.
Relentless, frothing breakers pounded the rocks, hurling spume high above the promontory.
The desolate, windswept strand stretched to the horizon, unmarked by a single footprint.
At the mouth of the bay, jagged, black outcrops loomed out of the surf like the ribs of a wrecked ship.
Tangled ropes of kelp and bleached, twisted driftwood littered the tideline, the debris of last night's storm.
The translucent, turquoise shallows glittered in the morning light, every pebble on the seabed sharply visible.
A languid, glassy swell rolled in, and each wave sighed across the sand before sinking away.
Damp, glistening shingle crunched beneath his boots as he followed the water's edge.
The wave gathered itself, broke, and receded with a long hiss, dragging the pebbles after it.
By dusk the tide had erased their footprints, and the beach lay as blank as if no one had ever walked there.
Tiny crabs scuttled into the rock pools at the first tremor of a footstep.
Each of the still, crystalline rock pools held a miniature world of anemones and darting shrimp.
Gulls wheeled and shrieked overhead, quarrelling over whatever the waves had surrendered.
A raw, salt-laden wind whipped across the dunes, flattening the marram grass and stinging every inch of bare skin.
Sheer, crumbling cliffs towered above the cove, shutting out the last of the daylight.
He clung to the slick rocks while the sea seethed around him, each surge threatening to prise his fingers loose.
Sea and sky merged at the hazy, indistinct horizon, so that distant ships seemed to hang in the air.
The path curved around the bay, rising and dipping with the low, grass-tufted dunes.
Her feet sank into the warm sand, and for the first time in weeks she felt her shoulders loosen.
She gathered tiny, iridescent shells, each one glowing like the inside of a pearl.
The storm drove the sea up the beach in grey, heaving walls that scoured the foreshore down to bare rock.
Out of season, the beach belonged to the wind, the gulls and one solitary walker.
Children shrieked as the surf chased them up the sand, then turned and chased it back.
The sharp, briny tang of seaweed hung in the air long before the sea itself came into view.
The tide was coming in fast, silently filling the channel between them and the shore.
At sunset the wet sand turned to beaten copper, and the retreating waves were edged with fire.
The whole bay basked in the afternoon sun, drowsy and still.
No road led to the remote, pebble-strewn inlet; it could be reached only at low tide, and only on foot.
